The declared 512-token function prompt budget is below the size of the prompt's own required sections, so raising it should increase reference-validity and Kill@k without changing evaluator semantics.
experiments.reason: CPU evidence narrows the admissible budgets to 1024 and above. It does not select one: which admissible budget yields better Kill@k and reference-validity is still an open GPU question. No budget has been selected and no model has been trained at any budget.

local_cpu_evidence.method: Section-aware compaction attempted for every function record on each panel. No model loaded, no GPU used. Exhaustive, not sampled.

experiments.protocol_note: The prompt budget is part of the evaluation scope hash. Results at a new budget are not comparable with V4 numbers produced at 512 unless the V4 adapter is re-evaluated under the same budget.
experiments.gate_conclusion: Promptability is a hard prerequisite, not a performance result. 512 fails on both panels. 768 clears val but leaves 28 unpromptable ablation_dev records. 1024 is the smallest tested budget that clears evaluation_panel_fully_promptable on both panels, and 1024+128 leaves ample room in the 2048 sequence budget. Excluding the 28 records to make 768 pass would silently change the panel and is not permitted.

experiments.hypothesis: A smaller code-specialised base model with an available fused-attention backend can raise reference-valid, execution-valid generation and cut generation cost without any change to the evaluation protocol.
experiments.training_size: zero-shot screen (no training); plus one 32-pair integration run for L2

integration_evidence_L2.monitor_gate_reason: end_to_end_candidate_kill_rate fell 0.277344 -> 0.253906, outside the monitor's 0.01 candidate-health tolerance, so the checkpoint was correctly not promoted. Function kill rate rose 21 -> 23 and McNemar exact p = 0.7266, so this 6-optimizer-step run carries no training signal either way.

experiments.result: L1 is impossible in the pinned environment. L2 beats L0 on every candidate-validity layer measured over 256 candidates per arm (parse 0.980 vs 0.508, execution 0.980 vs 0.410, reference 0.566 vs 0.270) and is 5.1x faster per function, while zero-shot function kill rate is higher (0.719 vs 0.594) with overlapping Wilson intervals on n=32.
experiments.reason: Accepted as the base model for subsequent experiments because the decision hierarchy ranks reference- and execution-validity above the headline kill rate, and those gaps are large and measured over 256 candidates per arm. The kill-rate gap alone would be inconclusive at n=32. This is not a trained-model result: no research-scale SFT comparison between the two base models exists. A base-model swap also changes the tokenizer, so the prompt-budget admissibility sweep and every V4 comparison must be re-derived before any headline claim.
negative_results_retained: L1 Phi-3 + SDPA: transformers 4.48.3 refuses SDPA for Phi3ForCausalLM; flash_attention_2 also unavailable for its sliding-window attention. Eager is the only admissible Phi-3 backend in this environment.
L2 32-pair integration did not pass the checkpoint-promotion gate; the candidate-health dip is retained rather than reported as a success.

Repeated identical-configuration runs did not reproduce bit-exactly: L0 Kill@1 moved 7/32 -> 5/32 and L2 baseline moved 23/32 -> 21/32 across processes at fixed seed, so single-run deltas below roughly two functions on this panel are not evidence.
